title: Criteria weights for traffic-safety scenario S1 with IMF SWARA

source.citation: Damjanović, M., Stević, Ž., Stanimirović, D., Tanackov, I., Marinković, D. (2022). Impact of the number of vehicles on traffic safety: multiphase modeling. Facta Universitatis, Series: Mechanical Engineering, 20(1), 177-197.
source.note: Worked example of IMF SWARA (Vrtagić et al. 2021, Axioms 10(2), 92, doi:10.3390/axioms10020092) by co-authors of the method. The Axioms paper's own tables could not be read (images on the publisher page).

input.criteriaOrder: descending significance, as ranked by the experts

deviations.note: 0.7778 / 3.3058 = 0.2353; Table 4 prints 0.23 where rounding gives 0.24. Other cells of the same table are rounded, not truncated.
Same value and same print as row 2.

notes: The scale TFNs are stored as exact fractions in double precision (2/9 = 0.2222...), as printed in Table 2.
Assessments were read back from the printed s_j triples of Table 4; the term with the matching TFN is recorded.

Crisp weights are the graded mean (l + 4m + u) / 6 of the fuzzy weights. The paper does not state the formula. The graded mean reproduces every printed crisp value; so does the centroid, so the choice follows Fuzzy MARCOS by the same authors (docs/methods/swara.md).
The crisp weights do not sum exactly to 1 (for example 1.0003 in S1) because defuzzification is not additive across the normalised fuzzy weights.
Scenarios S4 and S5 of the paper have the same assessment pattern and identical numbers, so they are not repeated as fixtures.
